answer: The wharf multiplier is published, charged in jetty, and zephyr lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 821 identities would post 3109 proofs and burn roughly 36 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
